The narrow case — an open `claude/implement-plan-*` PR with a blocking label (`ai:review-blocked`, `ai:review-autofix-failed`, or `ai:needs-human`) but no hold — therefore makes one paginated REST request per check-in that the previous code did not make. The changelog row "Extra GitHub API calls | 0 (the one comment listing is read once and reused for the hand-off check)" is inconsistent with the new code path: the listing is read in this case but never reused. The internal API-budget docstring at `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:84` ("read once, before the label check, for both the hold and the hand-off") already documents the new ordering; the changelog just needs to acknowledge that a blocking-label-without-hold fixer head pays the extra call. Runtime verdict (`state: blocked`, `done: true`) is correct; this is a documentation-precision gap, not a runtime defect.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
